rv.q: A gaggle of young gals at a nightclub, rub shoulders as they pass in and out of the toilets. Chatting, sharing and venting about their reasons for being there, they exude a vigorous vibrancy and very occasionally, a vituperative venom. Jazz Jenkins and April Hope Miller in FLUSH (c) Alex Brenner.
What unfolds is an ensemble comedy that’s both sharply funny and tender, capturing fleeting moments of connection that happen in unexpected places.
Miller’s debut announces a writer who knows what she wants to say and, more importantly, how to say it.

cn.t: Critics praise this sharply funny ensemble comedy set in a club bathroom, where honest confessions and fleeting connections between sixteen women create both tender and incisive moments that resonate with female audiences.
